summary: The article explores 'Phygital' language, the blending of physical and digital communication, tracing it from AIM-era chat to Instagram. It covers how slang, emojis, hashtags and memes have moved into everyday speech and across generations, citing several experts. It also notes the ephemeral nature of slang, shorter syntax, and the expressive power of silence.
one_line: An article on how digital slang, emojis, hashtags and memes are merging online and offline speech into 'Phygital' language.
key_facts: The article is dated September 17, 2024 and describes 'Phygital' as a blending of physical and digital worlds in language.
Dr. Sofia Moreno is credited with first coining the term 'Phygital' in her March 2025 TED Talk.

Jane Nguyen, a sociologist from the University of Communication Evolutions, said on October 3, 2024: "What we're witnessing is not just a trend; it's the emergence of a new linguistic ethos where expressions are concise, emotions GIF-able, and every word is potentially viral."
Words like 'lit', 'shade', 'salty' and 'ghosting' have moved from touchscreens into the speech of Gen-Xers and Baby Boomers.
Tech columnist Jamal Rogers published an 'Emoji Trend Report' on April 12, 2025, stating "The right emoji at the right time can speak louder than a paragraph of text."
Social media analyst Henry Bates said at a seminar that hashtags have infiltrated everyday speech as 'a form of metacommentary'.
The 'Meme Connoisseur's Annual Symposium' was held on January 15, 2025 in New York City, dedicated to memes as a digital dialect.
Professor Alex Keane said at the symposium: "Memes are the folklore of the online world, rapidly evolving narratives that are shared, disputed, and remixed."
Internet acronyms such as 'IRL' (in real life) and 'FOMO' (fear of missing out) now appear in business meetings, coffee shops and brunch conversation.
The word 'slay' has shifted from a fashion-world battle cry to a rallying call for anyone who excels.
Digital communication favors brevity, so sentence structures bend toward messages that are digestible, snackable and shareable.
Silence, ellipses and blank messages are described as having expressive power in Phygital communication.
